question: Can selecting only changed ANS detector streams reach an 8.33 ms interaction budget without changing existing GPU reduction bits?

parameters.control: QGPU_FLOAT_ANS_FULL_DECODE_CONTROL=1; same executable, existing full-window GPU decode
parameters.sequence: 96 identical aperture masks per arm; A/B/A per source; reset/large jump separate from steady drag
parameters.timer: encodeVirtualImage through command completion; CPU mask construction and output hash outside timer; GPU command timestamps separate
parameters.memory: ANS only; unchanged bounded query window; two image-sized accumulated sums; no full decoded duplicate
parameters.cache: fresh process/resident each arm; uncontrolled OS pages; not a cold SSD benchmark
parameters.stage_profile: Metal timestamp attachments on separate decode/reduction encoders; same numerical work, instrumented timings not used for a native FPS claim
parameters.direct_literal_probe: Consume independent literal/constant ANS codes directly in the unchanged compensated detector reduction; decode entropy columns only into bounded scratch. Specialize the legacy row-word accessor for already decoded words, not XOR packing.

final_candidate.post_build_edits: Kernel comment and Python docstring corrections only; no functional code change.

parallel_literal_probe.hypothesis: 32 scan lanes per selected literal/constant stream remove unnecessary sequential decoding while entropy streams retain the reference decoder

serial_encoder_probe.hypothesis: One serial encoder with explicit bounded-scratch barriers removes per-chunk encoder overhead

outputs.result: Frozen products remain byte-identical on three real sources. Candidate medians 6.252/6.257/1.736 ms; periodic rebases reach 104 ms. Native sustained 120 FPS is not qualified. All raw result hashes are retained in this artifact.
